edition.internalStatus: HY-1.0 LIVE · gate 25/25 PASS · revision #28 held (10/8/72/10) · quiet 0/10 · Kuwait class review flagged.

views.client: Stocks rallied in Friday's shortened session: the S&P 500 rose 1.6% and the Nasdaq 2.3%, led by chip stocks, and the S&P is back near its long-term trend line. Treasury yields rose, with the ten-year at 4.94%, and a December rate rise is almost fully priced. Oil was steady, with WTI at $83.08 and Brent at $95.44, after attacks on a Saudi refinery and near a tanker. Our reading stays DISINFLATION / HAWKISH PIVOT; two of four conditions are met.
views.internal: The market reversed the 200-day break within two sessions and the VIX fell below 25, so the equity scare that defined Wednesday has largely passed. The bond market did not join in: the ten-year rose 9bp and a December hike is all but certain, which is the hawkish half of our label doing its work. The geopolitical tape got worse, not better, with four executed attacks in two days, including two Italians killed in Kuwait.

drivers.b: S&P +1.60% to 7,297.49 in the half session, 0.69% under its 200-day: Market Structure back to Technical neutral after one session. VIX 23.81, below 25; Nasdaq +2.31%, all eleven sectors up.

drivers.t: Yields up with stocks; more Gulf attacks
drivers.b: 2Y 4.69 (+8bp), 10Y 4.94 (+9bp), December hike 98.9% priced. Jazan refinery hit and a Kuwait drone attack; Brent Jan 95.44, WTI reference 83.98. Weights held 10/8/72/10.
